name: Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: ILAR Classification Criteria for Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis

criteria.description: Arthritis in one or more joints persisting for at least 6 weeks
Onset of disease before 16 years of age
Exclusion of other known causes of arthritis such as infections, malignancies, or other rheumatic diseases
Presence or absence of systemic features such as fever, rash, or serositis to classify subtype

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Persistent arthritis for at least 6 weeks in one or more joints with onset before age 16 and exclusion of other causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Classification into subtypes depends on clinical features and laboratory findings.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Persistent joint swelling lasting more than 6 weeks
searchTerms: joint swelling lasting more than 6 weeks

pathognomonic.symptomName: Morning stiffness with limited joint mobility
searchTerms: stiff joints in the morning with limited movement
morning joint stiffness and reduced mobility

pathognomonic.symptomName: Chronic synovial inflammation confirmed by clinical examination
searchTerms: chronic joint lining inflammation confirmed clinically

common.symptomName: Limping or refusal to use affected limb
searchTerms: limping or not using one limb
refusal to walk on affected leg
uneven walking due to limb pain
arthritis affecting fewer than five joints
joint inflammation in a few joints
eye inflammation affecting the front of the eye

occasional.symptomName: Rash associated with systemic onset subtype
searchTerms: widespread rash in systemic onset disease
inflammation of heart lining or lung lining
pericarditis or pleuritis causing chest pain

rare.notes: Life-threatening complication mostly in systemic JIA
searchTerms: dangerous inflammation with fever and organ problems

laboratory: Elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) and C-reactive protein (CRP)
Negative rheumatoid factor in most subtypes except RF-positive polyarticular JIA
Antinuclear antibody (ANA) positivity in oligoarticular subtype
imaging: Joint space narrowing and erosions on X-ray in chronic disease
Ultrasound showing synovial hypertrophy and effusion
genetic: Association with HLA-DRB1 alleles in some subtypes
other: Synovial fluid analysis showing inflammatory profile

distinguishingFeatures: Rapid joint destruction without chronic inflammation
Multisystem involvement including renal and hematologic
Systemic symptoms like night sweats and weight loss

redFlags: High persistent fever with rash and organomegaly
Signs of macrophage activation syndrome (cytopenias, coagulopathy)
references: Petty RE, et al. International League of Associations for Rheumatology classification of juvenile idiopathic arthritis: second revision, Edmonton, 2001. J Rheumatol. 2004.
Giannini EH. Juvenile idiopathic arthritis: diagnosis and treatment. Rheum Dis Clin North Am. 2005.
